methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops by a Norfolk native directly combat concentration by building grassroots capability outside metro hubs, signaling peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could enable distributed deep adoption in underserved regions.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnering with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for deep AI capability in Richmond, but the metro-focused partnership model risks replicating the concentration pattern unless rural extension mechanisms are explicit.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National Hospital
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's pediatric AI collaboration with Children's National deepens research-grade capability in Blacksburg, but the specialized academic-medical focus suggests excellence clustering around flagship institutions rather than broad workforce distribution.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia signals bottom-up capability building in historically underserved coal transition regions, testing whether distributed deep adoption can take root outside traditional tech corridors.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Cavalier Daily op-ed explicitly diagnosing how NoVA data center concentration increases urban-rural divide signals awareness that current infrastructure investment patterns deepen rather than bridge the capability gap.
